questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from escaping the air brake system.
Stop air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from escaping the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must stay closed to prevent air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down on ramps and corners. Do not make quick lane changes with trailers.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Push the accelerator to the floor.

questions.explanation: To prevent tipping with a trailer, steer smoothly and gently. Avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, at what angle should the seals be pressed together?
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves and listen for air escaping. Then close both shut-off valves before driving.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full trailers attached.
questions.explanation: Bobtail tractors have no trailer attached. They are harder to stop and need more distance to come to a complete stop than tractors with loaded trailers.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, what following distance should you maintain for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: If you are backing and are unsure about your path, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and get out to look.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure of your path while backing, stop the vehicle and get out to check your path of travel.

questions.question: When backing your tractor to couple it to a trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Before backing under a trailer during coupling, lock the trailer brakes.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath can be difficult to drive over:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are hard to cross when pulling a trailer with low clearance. Single-axle tractors pulling long trailers and low-slung units have the most difficulty crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: If you press the tractor air supply control and the trailer's spring brakes do not release, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, make sure all equipment works properly. If the trailer's spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, check that the air line connections are connected and sealed correctly.

questions.question: What color identifies emergency or supply air lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded. Blue is used for service lines. Red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Then contact emergency services.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a combination vehicle turns too quickly. To prevent rollovers, keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is by:

options.text: Watching the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to see if your trailer is skidding or jackknifing is to watch it in your mirrors. This also helps you spot a skid as early as possible.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only when the trailer is carrying a load
Only to test the trailer's brakes
Only in bad weather when the trailer might skid

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer's brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: In a combination, place the heaviest-loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Place the lightest trailer at the rear.
